verdict.rationale: Rive documents an official MCP connection between the Rive Editor and AI tools, and RML gives coding agents a text-based representation of a Rive file. However, the documented MCP tools are write-oriented (creating View Models, State Machines, Layouts, Shapes) rather than pulling design context to implement elsewhere. Rive also has no HTTP API: the OpenAPI probes 404 and the served spec is a Mintlify sample. missing for 10: documented read access to frames/artboards, variables, screenshots, and component mappings via MCP or API; a real design-context API; independent or hands-on corroboration of an agent implementing a design from Rive context.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my coding agent can pull real design context — frames, variables, screenshots, component mappings — through an MCP server or API to implement the design

citations.quote: You can connect the Rive Editor to AI tools through MCP (Model Context Protocol).
official MCP server documented at https://rive.app/docs/editor/ai/mcp
The first set of tools are designed to let AI handle repetitive tasks, like creating complex View Models, State Machines with hundreds of states/layers, Layouts, Shapes, and more.
Rive Markup Language (RML) is a text-based representation of a Rive file.
